quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets during a crash.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Place inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Keep proper distance from other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep proper distance from other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation for group riding. Check your mirrors regularly. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Always maintain proper space between riders.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a serious head injury in a crash.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle's wind blast hits you, you will have the most room to correct your position if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space on both sides to recover if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black letters show traffic rules, like speed limits. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Is not safe for motorcyclists at any time.
Is usually safe unless the road is wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is usually safe unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. This area provides good traction when dry. When wet, avoid it. The strip is usually narrow enough to ride around it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you and helps prevent dehydration in warm weather. Many jackets are made to protect riders from overheating.

questions.question: When riding through a curve as a group, motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways. Staggered formation is used on straight roads.

questions.question: A larger cushion of space may not be necessary if:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when pavement is slippery, visibility is blocked, or traffic is heavy. You need less space only when conditions are ideal.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders behind them to watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is tailgating you. This warns them that you are about to slow down. It also alerts them to hazards ahead that you may be responding to.

questions.question: How much stopping distance does a motorcycle need in traffic?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs the same stopping distance as a car in traffic.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from having to chase the group and lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: What should you do if a small animal enters your lane while riding in traffic?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane if a small animal crosses. Swerving into other traffic can cause a crash with another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: How should you ride a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle handles differently than a two-wheeled bike. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: What brakes should you use for normal stops?

options.text: Both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping, even for normal stops. Make this a habit.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without forcing the inexperienced rider to lead.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, cover the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: To fit a passenger on your motorcycle, you may need to:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit at a different angle.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while braking on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: The minimum safe distance to stay behind another vehicle is _____ seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum of two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Use at least three seconds when conditions are poor, such as rain, fog, or night riding.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older is legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol level of ______ or higher.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with 0.08 percent blood alcohol or more is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, riders should use:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding on straight roads. However, switch to single-file when going through curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.
